about: The one list of Will Cook's websites, films and repositories. The home page at wcook04.github.io is built from it, and each website keeps a copy for its own header, footer and film slots. Edit this file, then follow README.md, 'Add a released film'.

owner.name: Will Cook
owner.lede: I’ve been using AI to do maths research and build software. As it produces more complicated work, I also want to make that work easier for other people to understand.
invitation: These videos show what I’ve learned to build. I’d love to put those skills to use on other problems. I’m looking for work, an internship, fellowship or funding, and I’m very open to working together. If there’s a problem you think I should try, please let me know.
If something doesn’t make sense, or you spot a mistake, please let me know. If your feedback leads to a change, I’d be happy to credit you, with your permission.

sites.name: Plectis Mathematics
sites.purpose: Eight Erdős problems I researched with AI, with the papers, computer-checked proofs of partial results and the approaches that failed.
sites.status: The original questions remain open where the problem pages say so.
sites.capture_caption: The front page of Plectis Mathematics, open at problem #68.

sites.name: Lean Exposition
sites.purpose: One result about the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model of magnets, explained three ways and linked to a map of the argument and its Lean statements.
sites.status: The three accounts are drafts. The site shows their reviews and what each check covers.
sites.capture_caption: The front page of the SK exposition, with its main theorem.

sites.name: Plectis Atlas
sites.purpose: Read OpenAI’s maths papers alongside the reports that outside groups wrote about their claims and proofs.
sites.capture_caption: The Atlas map: each circle is a subject and each dot a family of papers.

sites.name: Practical Formal Verification

routes.label: What each one is checked by

sites.purpose: 88 Python components from my research system. For twelve, mathematical proofs show that particular calculations follow precise written requirements.
sites.capture_caption: The system map: the 88 components in their seven families.

sites.name: Zenith
sites.purpose: Experiments on whether records of past mistakes help AI models test and repair code.
sites.status: Small research studies, with their limits described in the repository.
sites.capture_caption: The opening of the Zenith paper.

projects.name: Safety Core
projects.purpose: Keep agent rules in one file and see which are written instructions and which have a program checking commands.

projects.name: One Checkout
projects.purpose: Commit a selected change while other agents’ unfinished edits stay in the same files.

projects.name: Code Map
projects.purpose: Read saved descriptions of files and follow their recorded code connections in a map.

index_groups.title: Software and experiments with AI agents

repos.name: plectis-erdos
repos.description: Research on eight Erdős problems and the system behind it: Lean proofs, papers on research and writing, experiments and open questions.

repos.name: plectis-erdos-lean
repos.description: Lean 4 source for the eight Erdős problem programmes, with selected Comparator and Palomar checks.

repos.name: lean-exposition
repos.description: Pinned Lean evidence and traceable mathematical exposition, with an interactive reading website.

repos.name: plectis-atlas
repos.description: An independent reader for OpenAI’s mathematics release: papers, Lean statements and attributed outside readings.

repos.name: practical-formal-verification
repos.description: 88 Python components and worked examples for inspecting AI-assisted research.

repos.name: plectis-zenith
repos.description: Experiments on whether an AI tester finds more bugs after seeing its earlier misses, with studies of code repair.

repos.name: safety-core
repos.description: An editable rulebook and practical checks for coding agents.

repos.name: one-checkout
repos.description: Commit one agent’s fix without including another agent’s unfinished edits.

film_groups.title: Tools for working with AI agents

films.title: Introduction (V3): I still want to understand what AI builds
films.description: I use AI for maths research and software, and build interfaces so other people can follow the results.

films.title: Introduction (V1, older version): How the projects fit together
films.description: An older introduction. Watch the latest Introduction (V3) from the home page. I go through the maths, the code map, how I make these videos, and the tools I use to manage the agents. Then some research into how the agents could improve their own way of working.

films.title: Maths Map: eight Erdős problems on one map
films.description: I use Erdős #257 to show how to find a proof, its papers and an explanation video through the Maths Map.

films.title: Erdős #257: why some infinite sums cannot be fractions
films.description: I explain a known irrationality result for Erdős #257, starting with 1, 1/3, 1/7, 1/15, and so on.

films.title: Lean Exposition: read a maths paper beside its argument map
films.description: I show how to read a maths explanation beside a map of its assumptions, results and sources.

films.title: Spin glasses: how different can two nearly best answers be?
films.description: I explain how two nearly best arrangements of magnets can differ, starting with four arrows.

films.title: Atlas: why two people gave one OpenAI maths paper different verdicts on its completeness
films.description: I compare two checking reports for an OpenAI maths paper about pi, using Plectis Atlas.

films.title: Formal verification: what does this check actually prove?
films.description: I show what the proofs and saved checks cover in a map of 88 Python components.

films.title: Zenith: I showed an AI tester the bugs it missed
films.description: I test whether an AI code tester catches more bugs after seeing a record of its earlier misses.

films.title: Safety Core: my AI agent made up a setting to pass a test
films.description: I test written rules and command checks on a coding agent that tries to get past a failing test.

films.title: One Checkout: when Claude is done and Codex is still editing
films.description: I show how to commit one fix while another agent's unfinished edits stay in the same file.

films.title: CodeMap: finding my way through code written with AI
films.description: I follow a code search from a file's saved description to the function and the code that calls it.

films.title: Introduction (V2, older version): Using AI for maths research and software
films.description: An older introduction. Watch the latest Introduction (V3) from the home page. In this video I introduce the projects and explain how they fit together, from computer-checked proofs and papers to maps and videos you can follow yourself.
